title: I-Lang Protocol Specification
description:
I-Lang is an AI-native communication protocol that defines a formal vocabulary of 88 verbs, 29 core modifiers plus a 20-key media profile, 25 entities (17 addressable, 8 role), and 13 Greek aliases for structured communication between humans and AI, between AI agents, and within AI internal reasoning.

It introduces two syntaxes: operation syntax [] for executable instructions and declaration syntax :: for behavioral identity. Version 3.0 defines the communication format, version 4.0 adds execution semantics, and version 5.0 adds a trainable judgment layer built on an 11-dimensional judgment vector space governed by four axioms and a three-layer architecture, grounded in fuzzy mathematics.

I-Lang provides the semantic and judgment layer that sits above tool-integration protocols such as Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-discovery protocols such as Google's Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A). MIT licensed.

Release 4.1.0 adds the media profile on the v4 stable line as an expression-layer extension: a media profile of 20 keys counted separately from the closed core registry and in force only where an operation addresses a media artifact, and a media entity tier of three artifact targets. The 88 verbs, the 29 core modifiers, the Core, External and Role entity tiers and the v5.0 judgment layer are unchanged.

The media profile was first published on 2026-09-12 in release v5.0-pre.2.1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22728994) and is re-released here on the v4 line because it belongs to the expression layer. This release also files an open, non-normative proposal for region, mask and layer operations.
